task_name: nothing asks GitHub for `-REVIEW` any more

rubric.result: The objective promises three things and the diff produces all three. (a) The `-REVIEW` token leaves the backend: `GhPlanIssues.CHANGES_TOKEN` and `PlanIssueBody.CHANGES_LINE` are deleted, and the last remaining reference, `SliceSeed.GATES` in git-workspace.ts, drops the clause built from it; a grep of backend/src and backend/__tests__ now finds `-REVIEW` only inside the two new negative assertions that pin its absence. (b) The two gh calls behind it go: `changesArgvFor` (`issue view --json comments`) and `changesCommentArgvFor` (`issue comment --body -REVIEW …`), with `changesAsked`, `askChanges`, `#changesIn`, `#commentsIn` and `#demandRead`, and their two port methods `PlanIssues.changesAsked` / `askChanges`. (c) The exception family goes: `PlanChangesFailure`, `PlanChangesNotRead`, `PlanChangesNotUnderstood`, `PlanChangesNotAsked` are gone from exceptions.ts. `backend/API.md` still names `-REVIEW`, but that file is Task 8's (`### Task 8 — API.md no longer documents the retired endpoint`, **Files:** `backend/API.md`), so it is not owed here. Cross-check asked of me: the pull request's fix loop is untouched — `read-fixes-asked.ts`, `request-fixes`, `gh-pull-requests.ts`, `ct-api.ts` and `review-watch.ts` production appear nowhere in the diff — and `ChangeAsked` survives at backend/src/domain/value-objects/change-asked.ts, still constructed by `GhPullRequests.fixesAsked` (gh-pull-requests.ts:122); only the now-pointless `export { ChangeAsked }` re-export from gh-plan-issues.ts leaves with the method that justified it.

The **TDD:** line names `it('the_body_of_a_plan_issue_no_longer_invites_anyone_to_ask_for_changes_on_it')` in plan-issue-body.test.ts, asserting the rendered body carries neither `-REVIEW` nor the invitation sentence. The test in the diff (plan-issue-body.test.ts:297-304) builds the same input — `PlanIssueBody.of({ story: Opened.story(), comment: null })`, a rendered plan issue body — and asserts exactly that pair: `expect(body).not.toContain('-REVIEW')` and `expect(body).not.toContain('comment on this issue starting with')`, the second being the distinctive clause of the deleted `CHANGES_LINE` ('To ask for changes to the plan, comment on this issue starting with `-REVIEW`'). Same assertion, same input, same expected value, and red before the change, where `PlanIssueBody.CHANGES_LINE` was the second line of every body.

The brief carries one `Contract (backend/src/domain/ports/plan-issues.ts)` block and one `Current state (backend/src/infrastructure/gh-plan-issues.ts, lines 190-196)` block. The port after the diff is exactly the six methods the contract lists, in that order, with those parameter names and those return types: `open({ story, comment, repository }): Promise<PlanIssue>`, `claim({ issue, repository }): Promise<void>`, `requeue({ issue, repository }): Promise<void>`, `answerGo({ issueNumber, repository, nonce }): Promise<void>`, `storyOf({ issueNumber, repository }): Promise<UserStoryKey | UserStoryUrl | null>`, `statusOf({ issueNumber, repository }): Promise<PlanIssueStatusValue>` — `changesAsked` and `askChanges` are the only ones removed, and the `ChangeAsked` type import goes with them. The `Current state` block's `changesAsked` is gone from the adapter. The prose contract beside the blocks is honoured symbol by symbol: `GhPlanIssues` loses `CHANGES_TOKEN`, `changesCommentArgvFor`, `changesArgvFor`, `changesAsked`, `#changesIn`, `#commentsIn`, `#demandRead` and `askChanges`; `PlanIssueBody` loses `CHANGES_LINE` and the line it contributed to `of()`; plan-agent-brief.ts drops both sentences ending in `${PlanIssueBody.CHANGES_LINE}`; exceptions.ts loses the four named classes; `ChangeAsked` stays. The surviving error messages are unchanged verbatim (`gh issue view --json labels failed: …`, `… wears more than one status label (…)`), only the class thrown is renamed.

Four rows bear on this diff and each is implemented with its stated value. 'Which gh calls disappear' names `changesArgvFor`, `changesCommentArgvFor`, `CHANGES_TOKEN`, `#changesIn`, `#commentsIn`, `#demandRead`, `changesAsked`, `askChanges` and `PlanIssueBody.CHANGES_LINE` — all eight-plus-one are gone. 'Which exceptions disappear' names the four `PlanChanges*` classes and adds '`ChangeAsked` stays: `GhPullRequests.fixesAsked` is its other producer' — the four are gone and the value object stands. 'Which suite covers the surviving watch … No task may modify it' pins `backend/__tests__/infrastructure/pull-request-review-loop.test.ts`; it is not among the twelve touched paths and does not appear in the diff. D-8 ('The plan review retires and the review is the pull request') and D-15 ('nothing waits for an answer') are what make dropping the seeded invitation right rather than inlining it. No row is reopened.

conventions/defects.md, rule by rule. (1) Closed vocabulary: the subject is `GhPlanIssues.#statusIn`, whose dispatch over the status labels the diff leaves structurally intact — an unmapped label still raises instead of falling into a catch-all, and no loose string or boolean is introduced. Conforms. (2) Raw map as the return value of logic: no subject — nothing added returns or consumes a map; `#statusIn` still returns a `PlanIssueStatusValue`, and the code that built `ChangeAsked` value objects is deleted, not replaced by a map. (3) Two fields that have to agree, sentinels included: no subject — no field is added anywhere in the diff, and no absence is encoded as an empty string or a zero. (4) An error named for where it happens: this is the rule the new family answers to, and it answers it well. `PlanStatusNotRead` / `PlanStatusNotUnderstood` are named for what happens to the status read, not for the module that raises them, and they repair an inherited defect — `statusOf` was throwing `PlanChangesNotRead`, an error named for the `-REVIEW` comments it never reads. Conforms.
On the introduction of `PlanStatusFailure` weighed against conventions/simplicity.md ('the burden of proof is on what is added … which call breaks without it? Name it'): the calls are `GhPlanIssues.statusOf` (gh-plan-issues.ts:252-263, five throw sites), reached today by `ReadFixesAsked` (read-fixes-asked.ts:43) and `ReadImplementationProgress` (read-implementation-progress.ts:81), with `ReviewWatch.#sound` catching the family root (`if (!(cause instanceof PlanFailure)) throw cause`). `statusOf` survives in the Contract block, so deleting `PlanChangesFailure` forces a replacement. The cheaper routes do not exist: reusing `PlanIssueFailure` would drag both causes into `PlanCollapse.declaredFailures()` and change the API's refusal vocabulary, which no sentence of this slice asks for; reusing `PlanStoryFailure` would be the very defect rule 4 forbids; throwing bare `PlanFailure` would lose the two-cause split that conventions/domain.md prescribes ('A family of errors around one collaborator separates the two things it can do wrong') and that conventions/testing.md requires be told apart ('Both failure causes of every adapter are told apart in its tests' — pinned at gh-plan-issues.test.ts:563-564 and 571-572). The shape is a literal copy of `PlanStoryFailure` / `PlanStoryNotRead` / `PlanStoryNotUnderstood` two definitions above it in the same file, which is the in-repo exemplar. Burden discharged, and declared in the plan amendment as that document asks.
conventions/architecture.md: layering is respected and improved — git-workspace.ts (infrastructure) stops importing the `GhPlanIssues` adapter, and the new exceptions live in domain/exceptions.ts, the catalogue the repo already declares together. No new concept is smuggled into an old file: the family is three lines in the file that already holds all eighteen others. conventions/decisions.md: no rule is written twice; the deleted `-REVIEW` knowledge lived in one place and leaves in one move. conventions/boundaries.md: the two causes are still told apart at the adapter's edge and still reach only stderr, unchanged behaviour. conventions/style.md and the repo's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md English rule: the diff adds no identifier, test name or message outside English; `SliceSeed.GATES` remains Spanish prose seeded into a governed repo's SLICE.md, but that is pre-existing text the diff only shortens — translating it is not asked for by any sentence of this task and would itself be an `alcance` defect, so I record it here rather than as a finding. No delivery-shape rule of either yardstick bears on this diff: it is a pure removal behind no contract that crosses a process boundary (the two halves rule was spent in Tasks 1-3, per the plan's own row).

Every weakening `-` line traces to a sentence of the task. gh-plan-issues.test.ts loses the two describe blocks for `changesAsked` and `askChanges` with their `GhRecording` class, `changesAskedFor` / `changesRefusalFor` / `askChangesRefusalFor` helpers and the `A_CHANGE` fixture — the **Tests:** line names exactly this ('Removed on purpose: the `changesAsked`/`askChanges` describe blocks of `gh-plan-issues.test.ts` with their `changesAskedFor` and `askChangesRefusalFor` helpers'). The surviving status cases are rehoused under a new, accurate describe and keep every assertion, with only the class name renamed, including the two 'not an instance of the other' assertions. plan-issue-body.test.ts loses the asking-line describe, also named in **Tests:**; the incidental first-line assertion for a Jira story that rode along inside it is still covered by `a_plan_that_came_from_a_jira_story_is_read_back_as_that_story`, which round-trips through the rendered body, and by `a_story_line_pasted_inside_the_epic_context_is_not_read_back_because_only_the_first_line_counts`. plan-agent-brief.test.ts loses the `CHANGES_LINE` assertion (named in **Tests:**) and the `reviewErrandFor` describe, which goes because the method goes — `reviewErrandFor` has no reference left anywhere in backend/ after Task 4 removed `CmuxPlanAgents.review()`. plan-refusal.test.ts only renames the classes inside assertions of identical strength. git-workspace.test.ts drops `expect(gates).toContain('`-REVIEW`')` from a pre-existing test and replaces it with a dedicated test asserting the opposite — a strengthening of the pin, not a relaxation. review-watch.test.ts swaps the stand-in exception class without touching a single assertion.

The behaviour the objective promises is produced by production code, not by scaffolding. The `-REVIEW` token's disappearance is the deletion of `static CHANGES_TOKEN = '-REVIEW'` and `static CHANGES_LINE = …` in backend/src/infrastructure/gh-plan-issues.ts and of the `PlanIssueBody.CHANGES_LINE,` element from `PlanIssueBody.of()`'s returned lines; the seeded invitation's disappearance is the edit to `SliceSeed.GATES` in backend/src/infrastructure/git-workspace.ts; the gh calls and the exception family are deleted from production modules, and the port loses two real methods. Revert any of those production lines and both new tests go red. Nothing in the diff hard-codes an expected value in a double to stand in for a production line; the two new tests assert over strings the production code actually renders.

Every line inside the twelve files serves a sentence of the task, and nothing named in `### Out of scope` is touched: `ReadFixesAsked`, `RequestFixes`, `CtApi.#pullRequestReviews`, the go protocol's modules (`GO_TOKEN`, `goArgvFor`, `goBodyFor`, `answerGo`, `PlanGoNotAnswered` all stand byte for byte), `GATES.plan`, `POST /implement-plan` and `cmux-plan-agents.ts`. The three-path amendment to this task's own **Files:** is justified and adds, removes nothing. `backend/src/infrastructure/git-workspace.ts` built `SliceSeed.GATES` from `${GhPlanIssues.CHANGES_TOKEN}`, so the task cannot go green without it — typecheck breaks, and the task's own first verification command greps the whole of backend/src rather than only the listed files. Dropping the invitation clause rather than inlining a literal `-REVIEW` is the right of the two: the objective says the token leaves the backend, and D-8/D-15 make the sentence ('hasta entonces puede pedirte cambios comentando `-REVIEW` en el issue') a promise no longer kept, so inlining it would have seeded a lie into every governed repository while technically passing the greps. `backend/__tests__/infrastructure/review-watch.test.ts` imported `PlanChangesNotRead` purely as a stand-in `PlanFailure` subclass; it is the generic `ReviewWatch` suite, not the protected `pull-request-review-loop.test.ts`, which is untouched. `PlanAgentBrief.reviewErrandFor` leaves with the sentence the task ordered dropped and with its last caller, which conventions/simplicity.md requires ('A public symbol … with no caller' is an antipattern). The plan hunk, read line by line, changes only the **Files:** line (three additions) and adds three declaratory paragraphs; **TDD:**, **Tests:** and the five **Verification:** commands survive as unchanged context, so no control was disarmed by the amendment.

Two tests are added. `the_body_of_a_plan_issue_no_longer_invites_anyone_to_ask_for_changes_on_it` (plan-issue-body.test.ts:297-304) and `the_state_it_seeds_no_longer_invites_anyone_to_ask_for_changes_by_commenting_on_the_issue` (git-workspace.test.ts:583-590). Deterministic: both are pure string renders — no clock, no date, no network, no randomness, no sleep; the second reads `git.written[1][1]` from an in-memory `GitDouble`. Isolated: each constructs its own subject (`new GitDouble()`, a fresh `PlanIssueBody.of(...)`), mutates no shared state and depends on no ordering. Verifies real behaviour: both assert over text the production code renders, and each goes red if the production line this diff removed is restored — the first if `PlanIssueBody.CHANGES_LINE` returns to `PlanIssueBody.of()`, the second if the clause returns to `SliceSeed.GATES`; neither asserts on a mock's call count or on a constant the test defined. I loaded `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development` before looking for anything finer: both have clear behaviour-naming sentences, one behaviour each, no 'and' in the name, and no mock of the piece under test, so its 'Good Tests' table and its anti-pattern list give me nothing to pin. Nothing to report.
